changelog:
v6.0 — Sliding continuous lookback (regime_softness): the regime-adaptive momentum's hard fast/slow lookback gate becomes a continuous slide, closing the >10pp SPY-trailing calendar years (2019/2021/2023) and improving worst-3y-excess -22.3->-19.3 with RDD3y halved. Plus a market-keyed downtrend floor (m0.3): a graduated bond floor driven by the market's OWN realized-vol regime, so the crash-dodge no longer depends on which names momentum holds. D6 note: the sliding lookback lengthens the longest underwater stretch by 7 days (0.6%) — accepted deliberately as a negligible duration cost against the large trailing-consistency gains. Full-cycle vs v5.8: CAGR 20.7 (flat), Martin 5.81->~5.85, worst-12mo -4.2->~-3.6, maxDD -15.5->~-15.

[major: Two new mechanisms: continuous sliding-lookback (regime_softness) on the selection axis, and a market-vol-keyed downtrend bond floor (m0.3, D6-neutral dial) on the allocator axis — crash-dodge made menu-independent.]

[D6 regression accepted on longest underwater (d): The sliding lookback lengthens the worst underwater stretch by 7 days (1204->1211, +0.6%) while IMPROVING worst-3y-excess by 3pp (-22.3->-19.3), halving RDD3y (2.19->0.72), and closing the >10pp SPY-trailing years (2019/2021/2023). The m0.3 floor keeps worst-3y-excess better than v5.8. A 7-day duration change on a 3.3-year stretch is a negligible cost for the trailing-consistency gain plus menu-independent crash protection.]
